text.text_excerpt: I like this place for a lot of reasons. First and foremost, free wine tastings every Saturday!!! And you pour yourself. The wines available for sampling are first rate and very interesting. The selection for sale is nice too. Hopper's is not a huge place so the selection is a little small. And most of the wines are on the pricey side. But there are a decent amount of inexpensive selections though, just FYI, the lowest is probably about $10 and there are very few of those. The selection of wines from Burgundy is awesome. So check it out on Saturday and get some nice free wine.

A new wine store in Uptown is always a welcomed addition! Carte des Vins has a great selection of wines ranging from $10 to $70+. The staff is so helpful, and it's great to have people who really know their stuff. Since I am very to new to wine, the staff offered some great recommendations and can tell you the flavor profile of each wine. From time to time, Carte des Vins will offer free tastings. Tonight, I tried out their rosé tasting, and it was well attended with a great atmosphere. People got to sample six different rosé while listening to cheesy rock music (it was their theme). Since they are only a couple of weeks old, I have to spread the word about them. You gotta check them out!

I had read about Cartes Des Vins in the newspaper a while back about a special testing they were having. I couldn't make it that day, so I 'liked" them on Facebook to keep track of their tastings. Today, I was in the area and decided to stop in. They were having a tasting of 3 French wines and a sparkling white wine from Spain. I ended up buying a Cotes du Rhone I would have passed on the shelf if I hadn't tasted it first. I was impressed with their wide selection of French wines. I was surprised at how modest the prices were. I guess that's the advantage of visiting the source. When I'm in the area, it is worth stopping back in.
